svg.text: Grounding & RAG 📚 — giving the model facts it does not have
A model only knows what it learned in training, and that knowledge is frozen at the training date. Grounding means automatically
adding the missing facts into the prompt, so the correct answer becomes the most probable one.
🧊 The core problem: knowledge is frozen, and the model will not say "I don't know"
The model can only use what it saw in training. So it does NOT know: 🗓️ events after training · 🏢 your company's internal
docs · 🔒 personal / private data. And it was never trained to say "I don't know" — so it outputs the most probable words
instead, which can be confidently wrong. Three questions it cannot answer, but answers anyway:
❓ "Acme Corp's Q3 revenue?" (internal data) → 🤖 "$42.3M, up 8% YoY" ❌ invented
❓ "Who won the 2026 FIFA Women's Champions Cup?" (after training) → 🤖 "France" ❌ wrong
❓ "Drug interactions for metformin + lisinopril?" (no access) → 🤖 "Risk of acute hyperkalemic crisis" ❌
⭐ Why grounding works: the right context changes the probabilities (the key idea)
The model picks the next token by probability. If you put the right facts INTO the prompt, the right token becomes the most
probable one. Here is the SAME question — without context (left) vs with context added (right):
WITHOUT context → the model just guesses
next-token probabilities (spread out, top guess is only 11%):
France
Spain
Brazil
Argentina
England
WITH context added to the prompt → one clear answer
prompt now also contains this retrieved fact:
Arsenal won the 2026 FIFA Women's Champions Cup
Arsenal
✅ The right context makes "Arsenal" the obvious next token.
🛠️ Grounding = add the missing facts automatically. The 4 main ways
You already do a manual version when you paste code or files to debug. But that breaks when the docs are too large, there
are too many, or they keep changing. Grounding does it automatically:
🔍 RAG
Pull document chunks from a
vector DB that are similar to your
question, and add them to the prompt.
🌐 Web search
Do a live search and add fresh,
up-to-date web results to the
prompt.
🧰 Tool use (agents)
Let the model call tools — APIs,
code, or databases. (Search is
just one popular tool.)
🕸️ Knowledge graph
Feed structured facts: entities
and their relationships (linked
facts).
🔁 The RAG pipeline (the dominant method), step by step
1 · Chunk + embed
all docs → Vector DB
2 · Search the DB
with the user's query
3 · Pick top-K chunks
most similar (e.g. K = 3)
4 · Paste into context
chunks + the query
5 · LLM answers
using query + retrieved facts
✅ Does RAG help? Yes. A systematic review (2020 → May 2025) found RAG consistently reduces hallucinations, especially outdated knowledge.
⚠️ But RAG is NOT error-free — it only injects extra text into the context. 3 ways it fails
🟥 Bad docs: if the retrieved document is wrong, the model trusts it and gives a wrong answer.
📑 Contradictory docs
Q: "How do I authenticate to our internal API?" RAG retrieves BOTH: api-docs-v1.md (2021) "use token auth" AND
api-migration-guide-v2.md (2023) "token auth is deprecated". The model mixes them → says "both formats are supported" ❌
✂️ Poorly chunked docs
Q: "How do I handle a RateLimitError?" A naive split put the warning in Chunk A (score 0.91, picked): "retrying now = permanent ban".
But the FIX ("wait 30s, then retry") sits in Chunk B (score 0.6, NOT picked). So the model says you cannot recover ❌ — the chunking lost the answer.
🎯 Attention is biased: "lost in the middle"
Researchers found models pay the most attention to the beginning and the end of the
context window, and tend to miss things in the middle. So WHERE you place a document
matters — not just whether it is there.
high attention 👀
↑ start of context
middle
(easily ignored)
↓ end of context
high attention 👀
⟵ "Lost in
the middle"
🧰 The fix discipline: "Context engineering"
🧹 Curate: use a few GOOD docs, not many mixed good-and-bad ones.
🧱 Chunk well: split documents in a smart, meaning-aware way — not naive half-half cuts.
📍 Position for attention: put the most important docs at the START and END, where attention is highest.
🪧 Important: RAG is "soft conditioning", not a hard rule
The model CAN ignore the retrieved context and fall back to training. Example: "What is OpenAI's newest model?" — the context
says one thing, but the model may still answer "GPT-3.5 Turbo" from training. It weighs grounding vs training probabilities.
📡 2026 reality check
🏗️ "Context engineering" is now a #1 named challenge for enterprise AI teams (with hallucinations) — managing what goes into
the context window at scale is the real work.
🎯 "Lost in the middle" comes from positional bias (e.g. RoPE decay) and a U-shaped attention curve. As of 2026, no production
model has fully fixed it — even with 1M-token windows, position still matters.
🥇 The standard fix is a reranker: it re-scores the chunks and puts the single most relevant one at the TOP of the context,
where the LLM looks hardest. For medical / legal / financial use, teams add extra validation on top of RAG.
🔑 The one idea to keep:
"The right context makes the right tokens more probable." That is the whole game. The prompt is the conditioning
for the autoregressive loop, and "lost in the middle" is literally a bias inside the attention mechanism.
Next up: the model builds its OWN context by reasoning step by step (chain of thought).
